Rashi on Chullin 39a:10:1.hebrew: אלא זביחה דעבודת כוכבים דמיתסרא - בהנאה, כדאמרינן במסכת עבודה זרה (דף כט:): תקרובת עבודת כוכבים מיקרי "זבחי מתים", כדכתיב "ויאכלו זבחי מתים". מה מת אסור בהנאה, אף תקרובת עבודת כוכבים אסורה בהנאה. ומת גופיה מנלן דאסור בהנאה? אתיא "שם שם": נאמר כאן "ותמת שם מרים", ונאמר להלן גבי עגלה ערופה "וערפו שם את העגלה". מה עגלה ערופה אסורה בהנאה, כדאמר שם "תהא קבורתה", אף מת אסור בהנאה. ומה מת אסור בהנאה ומטמא באהל, אף תקרובת עבודת כוכבים נמי:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:10:1.english: Rather, the slaughter of idolatry, which is prohibited - From deriving benefit, as we say in tractate Avodah Zarah (page 29b): An offering to an idol is called "sacrifices of the dead," as it is written, "And they ate the sacrifices of the dead" (Psalms 106:28). Just as a corpse is forbidden for deriving benefit, so too an offering to an idol is forbidden for deriving benefit. And from where do we know that a corpse itself is forbidden for deriving benefit? It is derived through a verbal analogy of "there, there": It is stated here, "And Miriam died there" (Numbers 20:1), and it is stated elsewhere, regarding the heifer whose neck is broken, "And they shall break the heifer's neck there" (Deuteronomy 21:4). Just as the heifer whose neck is broken is forbidden for deriving benefit, as [the Gemara] says there, "Let its burial be [the same as that of a corpse]," so too a corpse is forbidden for deriving benefit. And just as a corpse is forbidden for deriving benefit and conveys impurity in a tent, so too an offering to an idol [is forbidden and conveys impurity in a tent].

Rashi on Chullin 39a:11:1.english: Rather, it is obvious - This statement, "thought does not disqualify in non-sacred animals," is speaking of thought from one service to another.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:11:2.hebrew: שמחשבה פוסלת במוקדשין - כדפרישית, דעיקר פיגול מעבודה לעבודה הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:11:2.english: That intent disqualifies in the case of consecrated animals - As I explained, that the essence of *piggul* [improper intent] is from one service to another.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:11:3.hebrew: אלא באותה עבודה בלבד - אם אמר שחיטה עצמה לעבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:11:3.english: Rather, only regarding that same service - If he said [that he is slaughtering] for idolatry, [with the intent that] the slaughter itself [is for the idol]:

Rashi on Chullin 39a:12:1.hebrew: פנים קשיא לריש לקיש - דקתני "מחשבה פוסלת במוקדשין" ולא קתני "מפגלת", ש"מ בשאר פסולי פנים נמי, כגון זריקת דם וחטאת שלא לשמה, קתני דמחשבין:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:12:1.english: The inside [case] is difficult for Reish Lakish - For [the mishna] taught, "Intent disqualifies [offerings] in the case of consecrated animals," and did not teach "renders piggul." [We may] infer from this that with the other disqualifications of inside [service] as well, such as the sprinkling of the blood and a sin-offering [brought] not for its own sake, [the mishna] teaches that one can have [disqualifying] intent.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:12:2.hebrew: חוץ קשיא לרבי יוחנן - דקתני הכא בחולין, אין מחשבה פוסלת מעבודה לעבודה:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:12:2.english: "Outside" is difficult for Rabbi Yochanan - Because it teaches here, regarding non-sacred animals, that [improper] intent does not disqualify [the offering] from one service to another.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:13:1.hebrew: בשלמא פנים לר"ל לא קשיא - דאיכא למימר, מקמי דשמעה להך מתניתין מרבי יוחנן רביה, הוה פליג אסברא דרביה ואמר, מסתברא דלא ילפינן. ולבתר דשמעה להך מתניתין מרבי יוחנן רביה, וידע דלאו סברא דרבי יוחנן רביה אלא מתניתא הוא דגמרינן פסול מפיגול, איכא למימר דהדר ביה. להכי נקט רבי יוחנן, משום דרביה הוה ואגמריה משנה וברייתא. ל"א: לבתר דשמעה לרבי יוחנן רביה דפליג עליה ואמר "מחשבין", איכא למימר דהדר ביה:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:13:1.english: Granted, [the case of] inside is not difficult for Reish Lakish - For one can say that before he heard this mishna from Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher, he disagreed with his teacher's reasoning and said, "It is logical that we do not derive [it]." But after he heard this mishna from Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher, and knew that it was not the reasoning of Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher, but rather a mishna from which we derive that disqualification [applies] from piggul, one can say that he retracted. Therefore it mentions Rabbi Yochanan (as the one he heard it from), because he was his teacher and had taught him mishna and baraita. Another explanation: After he heard Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher, who disagreed with him and said, "One transfers intent [from one service to another]," one can say that he retracted.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:14:1.hebrew: בארבע עבודות - הא דקתני "אין מחשבה פוסלת בחולין", לאו מעבודה לעבודה קאמר, אלא בארבע עבודות קאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:14:1.english: In the four services - That which [the mishna] taught, "Thought does not disqualify [animals slaughtered as] non-sacred," does not mean [that thought is ineffective] from one service to another; rather, it means [that thought is ineffective] with regard to the four services.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:14:2.hebrew: וה"ק ומה - מוקדשין שנפסלין במחשבה בארבע עבודות, שחיטה וקבלה זריקה והולכה, באיזו מאלו שחישב ע"מ לאכול מן הזבח חוץ לזמנו, פיגול הוא. אין מחשבה הולכת אלא אחר העובד:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:14:2.english: And this is what it means: And if - Consecrated animals, which are disqualified through intention in the four services (slaughter, receiving, sprinkling, and carrying), in whichever of these one intended to eat from the offering outside its proper time, it is piggul. Intention goes only after the one who performs the service.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:1:1.hebrew: לא ילפינן - למימר בעלים אוסרין, אלא כדכתיב קרא (תהילים ק״ו:כ״ח) "זבחי מתים", שנזבח לעבודת כוכבים. דבפנים הוא דכתיב (במדבר ט״ו:ד׳) "והקריב המקריב", דבעלים קרי "מקריב". אבל בחוץ לא אמרינן הכי:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:1:1.english: We do not derive - To say that the owners render [the offering] forbidden, except as the verse states (Psalms 106:28) "sacrifices of the dead," meaning that it was sacrificed to idolatry. For it is with regard to the inside [of the Temple] that it is written (Numbers 15:4) "And the one who offers shall bring near," as the owner is called "one who offers." But with regard to the outside, we do not say this.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:1:2.hebrew: ור"א סבר ילפינן - במה מצינו, דבעלים פוסלים במחשבת עבודת כוכבים בחולין, ואפילו אחר שוחט; וגבי עובד כוכבים אפילו בסתמא, דסתם מחשבת עובד כוכבים לעבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:1:2.english: And Rabbi Eliezer holds that we derive - [By the method of] "in what do we find": [that] the owners disqualify through the intention of idolatry in non-sacred animals, even if another person slaughters; and in the case of a gentile, even without a specific statement, for the unspecified intention of a gentile is for idolatry.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:1:3.hebrew: זה מחשב וזה עובד לא אמרינן - דהמקריב לא יחשב מקריב ממש, קאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:1:3.english: One thinks and another performs the service – we do not say - He means that the one who offers the sacrifice is not considered to be actually offering it.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:2:1.hebrew: לזרוק דמה לעבודת כוכבים - ודאשחטה לשם עבודת כוכבים, שהיה בדעתו לעובדה בשחיטה זו, דברי הכל אסורה, דהא זבחי מתים הוא. אלא בשלא היה מתכוין להיות שחיטה זו עבודה לעבודת כוכבים, אלא שחטה לעצמו ע"מ שיעבוד העבודת כוכבים בזריקת דמה או בהקטר חלבה:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:2:1.english: To throw its blood for idolatry - For if he slaughtered it for the sake of idolatry, [meaning] that he intended to worship [the idol] with this very slaughter, everyone agrees that it is forbidden, for it is a "sacrifice of the dead." Rather, [the case here] is where he did not intend for this slaughter to be an act of worship for idolatry, but slaughtered it for himself, on the condition that he would worship the idol through the throwing of its blood or the burning of its fats.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:2:2.english: Invalid - It is forbidden to derive benefit from it:

Rashi on Chullin 39a:3:1.hebrew: מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - כשחישב בשעת עבודה זו על עבודה אחרת, כגון שחישב בשחיטה על הזריקה, הויא מחשבה לגבי עבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:3:1.english: We may have intention from one service to another - When, during the time of this service, one had in mind another service, for example, if during the slaughter one had in mind the sprinkling, it constitutes [a valid] intention with regard to idolatry.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:3:2.english: For we derive "outside" - [Meaning, the prohibition of] idolatry.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:3:3.hebrew: מפנים - ממחשבת פיגול של פנים, שהשוחט ע"מ לזרוק דם למחר או להקטיר אימורין למחר, זהו עיקר פיגול:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:3:3.english: From within - From the intention of piggul of the inside [i.e., of offerings whose blood is brought inside], where one slaughters with the intention to throw the blood tomorrow or to burn the sacrificial parts tomorrow. This is the essential case of piggul.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:5:1.hebrew: שחטה לשמה - בחטאת מיירי, דכל שאר זבחים כשרין שלא לשמן, אבל חטאת שנשחטה שלא לשמה פסולה, וכן פסח שנשחט שלא לשמו. ואם שחט החטאת לשמה לזרוק דמה שלא לשמה:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:5:1.english: If he slaughtered it for its own sake - [The Gemara] is speaking of a sin-offering, for all other sacrifices are valid when slaughtered not for their own sake, but a sin-offering that was slaughtered not for its own sake is invalid, and so too a Paschal offering that was slaughtered not for its own sake. And [the case is] where he slaughtered the sin-offering for its own sake, intending to sprinkle its blood not for its own sake.

Rashi on Chullin 39a:6:1.hebrew: רבי יוחנן אמר פסולה - דגמרינן מחשבת פסול שלא לשמה ממחשבת פיגול, דעיקרו מעבודה לעבודה:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:6:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says it is disqualified - For we derive the thought of disqualification [by slaughtering] not for its own sake from the thought of piggul, whose main [case] is [a thought held] during one service [concerning] another service:

Rashi on Chullin 39a:7:1.hebrew: וצריכא - לאשמועינן בתרווייהו מחלוקת דרבי יוחנן ור"ש:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:7:1.english: And it is necessary - To teach us the dispute of Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish in both [cases].

Rashi on Chullin 39a:7:2.hebrew: דאי איתמר בהא - מילתא קמייתא, דהשוחט את הבהמה:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:7:2.english: For if it had been stated with regard to this - The first matter, [that of] one who slaughters the animal [with the intent to throw its blood to an idolatry].

Rashi on Chullin 39a:7:3.english: In this case Reish Lakish said [it] - That one does not transfer [intent] [from one service to another]:

Rashi on Chullin 39a:7:4.hebrew: פנים מפנים - פסול דחטאת שלא לשמה מפיגול:
Rashi on Chullin 39a:7:4.english: Inside from inside - The disqualification of a sin-offering [slaughtered] not for its own sake [is derived] from [the disqualification of] piggul.

Tosafot on Chullin 39a:10:1.hebrew: אלא זביחה דעבודת כוכבים דמיתסרא היכי משכחת לה - תימה, אי חשיב פיגול אף במחשבה בלא דיבור, אם כן משכחת זביחת עבודת כוכבים דמתסרא בדיבור, שפירש בפירוש ששוחט לעבודת כוכבים:
Tosafot on Chullin 39a:10:1.english: Rather, [regarding] the slaughter for idolatry, how is it found that it becomes forbidden? - It is astonishing: if it is considered piggul even through thought alone, without speech, then if so, [how] is the slaughter for idolatry found to be forbidden through speech, [that is, where the slaughterer] explicitly stated that he is slaughtering for idolatry?

Tosafot on Chullin 39a:12:1.hebrew: פנים קשיא לר"ש בן לקיש - פירש בקונטרס דלא מצי למימר ק"ו שלו מפגול, דלא הויא ליה לומר פוסלת אלא מפגלת. ואע"ג דמצינו דקרי ליה לפיגול פסול, דתניא בפ"ב דזבחים (דף כח.) חוץ למקומו פסול ואין חייבין עליו כרת, הכא דאיכא למטעי ה"ל למיתני מפגלת, כדאמרינן בפ"ב דזבחים (גם זה שם) גבי הא דתנן שהזבח נפסל בד' דברים כו', ודייק בגמרא, דיקא נמי דקתני שהזבח נפסל ולא קתני שהזבח מתפגל. אבל קשה, אמאי לא מוקי לה בשינוי בעלים, דמודה ר"ל דמחשבינן מעבודה לעבודה אם אמר הריני שוחט ע"מ לזרוק דמו לשם פלוני דפסול, כדאמרינן בפרק ב' דזבחים (ג"ז שם). לכ"נ דליכא לאוקמי ק"ו לא במחשבת פיגול ולא בשינוי בעלים, דמה לתרווייהו שכן אינן באותה עבודה, שאם אמר הריני שוחט לשם חוץ לזמנו או חוץ למקומו או לשם פלוני כשר, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דזבחים (דף י.). ורבינו חננאל גריס פנים לריש לקיש לא קשיא, דמוקי לה במחשבת פיגול:
Tosafot on Chullin 39a:12:1.english: "Penim" is difficult for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres that he cannot state his a fortiori argument from piggul, because he should not have said "disqualifies" but rather "makes piggul." And even though we find that [the Mishnah] calls piggul "disqualified," as it is taught in the second chapter of Zevachim (28a): [Slaughtering with the intent to offer] outside its place is disqualified, and one is not liable to karet for it; here, where there is room for error, [the Tanna] should have taught "makes piggul," as we say in the second chapter of Zevachim (ibid.) regarding that which we learned that the sacrifice is disqualified through four things, etc., and the Gemara infers: This is indeed precise, for it teaches that the sacrifice "is disqualified" and does not teach that the sacrifice "becomes piggul." But it is difficult: why does it not establish it [as referring] to a change of owner (shinui ba'alim), for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish concedes that we reckon [intent] from one service to another? [That is,] if one said, "I am slaughtering in order to throw its blood for the sake of so-and-so," it is disqualified, as we say in the second chapter of Zevachim (ibid.). Therefore it seems to me that it is impossible to establish the a fortiori argument [as referring] either to the intent of piggul or to a change of owner, for [one can respond]: What is true of both of them is that they are not in the same service, for if one said, "I am slaughtering for the sake of [eating] outside its time," or "outside its place," or "for the sake of so-and-so," it is valid, as we say in the first chapter of Zevachim (10a). And Rabbeinu Chananel has the text: "Penim" is not difficult for Resh Lakish, for he establishes it [as referring] to the intent of piggul:

Tosafot on Chullin 39a:12:2.hebrew: חוץ קשיא לרבי יוחנן - וא"ת, ולימא דקאי רבי יוחנן כרבנן, דכי היכי דילפי רבנן חוץ מפנים לענין דזה מחשב וזה עובד, ה"נ ילפינן לענין דמחשבין מעבודה לעבודה? וללישנא בתרא, לימא דקאי כר"א? וי"ל, דלגבי זה מחשב וזה עובד שייך למילף חוץ מפנים, דגלי רחמנא בפנים דבעלים קרוי מקריב, והוא הדין בחוץ, דכתיב (תהלים קו) זבחי מתים, דאם בעלים מחשבין חשיב זבחי מתים, כיון דבעלים קרוי מקריב בפנים; ואין זה אלא גילוי מילתא בעלמא. אבל לענין דמחשבין מעבודה לעבודה, לא אשכחינן דילפינן כלל, והא דמחשבין בפנים גזירת הכתוב בעלמא הוא:
Tosafot on Chullin 39a:12:2.english: [The case of] outside [the Temple] is difficult according to Rabbi Yochanan - And if you ask: But let us say that Rabbi Yochanan stands with the Rabbis, [namely] that just as the Rabbis derive [the law of] outside from inside with regard to [the case where] one [person] intends [the sacrifice] and another performs the service, so too we derive with regard to [the rule] that one may intend from one service to another? And according to the latter version, let us say that he stands with Rabbi Elazar? And one can answer: With regard to [the case where] one intends and another performs the service, it is appropriate to derive [the law of] outside from inside, because the Merciful One revealed regarding inside that the owner is called the one who brings the offering (maqriv), and the same applies outside, as it is written (Psalms 106), "the sacrifices of the dead" — [meaning] that if the owners' intentions are effective, it is deemed "sacrifices of the dead," since the owner is called the one who brings the offering inside; and this is merely a disclosure of a matter [that was already the case]. But with regard to [the rule] that one may intend from one service to another, we do not find that we derive [it] at all, and the fact that one may intend [from one service to another] inside is merely a scriptural decree.

Tosafot on Chullin 39a:13:1.hebrew: הא מקמי דשמעיה מר' יוחנן - תימה, מאי תירוץ הוא זה שמתרץ שאמר ריש לקיש קודם שלמד המשנה:
Tosafot on Chullin 39a:13:1.english: This was before he heard it from R. Yochanan - It is astonishing: what kind of answer is this that [the Gemara] gives, [namely] that Resh Lakish said [his view] before he learned the Mishnah?

Tosafot on Chullin 39a:2:1.hebrew: ריש לקיש אמר מותרת - מודה ר"ל דחייב מיתה, כדאמרינן בפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין סא.), מידי דהוה אמשתחוה להר, דהר מותר ועובדו בסייף. ואין לתמוה היאך נהרג, הא דלמא מימלך ולא זריק דם לעבודת כוכבים, כדאמרינן בפרק ד' מיתות (ג"ז שם:) דמסית שאמר אלך ואעבוד פטור, דמימלך ולא עביד. הכא ודאי לא מימלך, כיון דעביד מעשה ששחט ע"מ לזרוק. ועוד, דהכא אפילו ידוע ודאי שלא יזרוק חייב, דחשיב עובד עבודת כוכבים בשחיטה זו מה ששוחט ע"מ לזרוק:
Tosafot on Chullin 39a:2:1.english: Reish Lakish says it is permitted - Reish Lakish concedes that [the slaughterer] is liable to death, as we say in the chapter of "Arba Mitot" (Sanhedrin 61a), just as in the case of one who bows down to a mountain, where the mountain is permitted but its worshipper is [executed] by the sword. And one should not wonder how he is put to death, [given that] perhaps he would reconsider and not throw the blood to idolatry, as we say in the chapter of "Arba Mitot" (ibid. 61b) that an enticer [to idolatry] who said "I will go and worship" is exempt, because he may reconsider and not do it. Here, certainly he will not reconsider, since he has performed an act, [namely] that he slaughtered in order to throw. Moreover, here, even if it is known for certain that he will not throw, he is liable, because through this slaughter he is considered as one who worships idolatry, as he slaughters in order to throw.
